data.output:
{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

#flux: --job-name=NN_03-01
#flux: --output=output/NN_03-01-{{id}}.out
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 5
#flux: --time-limit=20h

# Note: LSF -q directive (gpuv100) does not have a direct Flux equivalent.
# Performance consideration: Queue selection not preserved. Job may run on different hardware.
# Note: LSF -gpu directive requests 1 GPU with exclusive_process mode.
# You may need to use 'flux mini submit -g 1' or '--gpus-per-node=1' at submission time.
# Performance consideration: GPU allocation not specified in batch script. Job may not have access to GPUs.
# Note: LSF exclusive_process mode does not have a direct Flux equivalent.
# Performance consideration: GPU sharing/isolation settings not preserved.
# Note: LSF -R "span[hosts=1]" ensures all tasks on one node.
# Flux -N 1 with -n 5 achieves similar behavior (1 node with 5 tasks).
# Note: LSF -R "rusage[mem=6GB]" requests 6GB memory per core (30GB total for 5 cores).
# Performance consideration: Memory limits not enforced. Job may be killed if exceeding node memory.
# Note: LSF -B (email on job start) does not have a direct Flux equivalent.
# Performance consideration: Email notifications not available.
# Note: LSF -N (email on job end) does not have a direct Flux equivalent.
# Performance consideration: Email notifications not available.
# Note: Flux uses {{id}} for job ID substitution instead of %J.

module purge
#module load tensorflow/1.5-cpu-python-3.6.2
module load tensorflow/1.5-gpu-python-3.6.2


for drop in 0.2 0.25 0.3 0.4
do
	for N in 250 350 400 450 550
	do
		for nhidden in 6
		do
			for act in sigmoid
			do
				for folder in 03-01-2019\ 11.04 09-01-2019\ 12.57 11-10-2018\ 11.36
				do
					for func in group_period_x_group_period group_period_2x2 atomic_number
					do
						python3 NN/NN_script.py $drop $N sigmoid 6 $folder $func
					done
				done
			done
		done
	done
done
"
}

You MUST not make up directives that do not exist.
